        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"

          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. # Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"

          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): ... wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch..."). This is dead/misleading documentation. The step name references "via PR" which no longer happens. This is an IMPORTANT maintainability issue.

3. **Duplicate `git fetch origin main`**: Guard 1 already runs `git fetch origin main` just before. The new code does `git fetch origin main` again immediately after. Redundant. SUGGESTION.

4. **The push doesn't verify what it pushes**: Previously guard 2 re-checked `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` after waiting for checks. Now after `git rebase origin/main`, it pushes HEAD:main unconditionally — the rebase may succeed and the pushes whatever HEAD is, which includes the versions.json bump commit. Wait — after rebase onto origin/main, HEAD contains main + the bump commit, so push is fast-forward. That's fine. But what if the rebase introduces conflicts? `git rebase origin/main` — since the only local commit is the versions.json bump commit on top of fetched main, and we fetched origin/main in guard 1, the rebase should be trivial. If there were a conflict, rebase would fail with non-zero exit and `set -euo pipefail` would kill the step — release fails after packs are published but before the ledger lands and before the GitHub Release is created. Hmm, is that a failure mode? The old code's philosophy was "never fail the release AFTER publishing". Here the release (GitHub Release publish) happens in the NEXT step, so failing here means no release published — actually failing here means packs were built but no release published and no ledger landed. The old comment said "never fail the release AFTER publishing" — the ledger push happens BEFORE "Publish the GitHub Release". All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. # Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"

          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main

            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

blocks.text:
Now let me analyze this PR carefully. It's a workflow change to `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml`. The change replaces the chore PR path (branch + PR + wait for checks + merge) with a direct push to main using a ruleset bypass actor.

Key observations:

1. **Workflow/CI safety dimension** is critical here.

2. The step name and comment are now stale: the step is named `"Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"` and the big comment block above still describes the PR-based approach ("Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors... the bump rides a side branch + PR + squash merge... Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): ... wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch..."). This is dead/misleading documentation. The step name references "via PR" which no longer happens. This is an IMPORTANT maintainability issue.

3. **Duplicate `git fetch origin main`**: Guard 1 already runs `git fetch origin main` just before. The new code does `git fetch origin main` again immediately after. Redundant. SUGGESTION.

4. **The push doesn't verify what it pushes**: Previously guard 2 re-checked `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` after waiting for checks. Now after `git rebase origin/main`, it pushes HEAD:main unconditionally — the rebase may succeed and the pushes whatever HEAD is, which includes the versions.json bump commit. Wait — after rebase onto origin/main, HEAD contains main + the bump commit, so push is fast-forward. That's fine. But what if the rebase introduces conflicts? `git rebase origin/main` — since the only local commit is the versions.json bump commit on top of fetched main, and we fetched origin/main in guard 1, the rebase should be trivial. If there were a conflict, rebase would fail with non-zero exit and `set -euo pipefail` would kill the step — release fails after packs are published but before the ledger lands and before the GitHub Release is created. Hmm, is that a failure mode? The old code's philosophy was "never fail the release AFTER publishing". Here the release (GitHub Release publish) happens in the NEXT step, so failing here means no release published — actually failing here means packs were built but no release published and no ledger landed. The old comment said "never fail the release AFTER publishing" — the ledger push happens BEFORE "Publish the GitHub Release". So failing the step on rebase conflict means the release never publishes even though packs were built. But with the concurrency group and fetch right before, conflicts are near-impossible unless... actually the local HEAD after `git reset --hard origin/main` in the "Sync to current main" step, plus one commit. Rebase onto freshly fetched origin/main — the delta is commits that landed between. Conflict on versions.json possible if two releases ran concurrently? Concurrency group serializes them, so no. Manual dispatch targeting non-main ref could... but then the guard `git diff HEAD origin/main` might pass or not. Edge-case.

Actually wait — more significant: with `set -euo pipefail`, if `git rebase origin/main` fails (conflict), the step fails → workflow fails → release NOT published → next push re-triggers. Is that bad? The PR description says "rejected push warns and the next release recomputes" — but a rebase conflict doesn't warn, it hard-fails. Given the fetch happens seconds before push, the window is tiny, and GitHub rejects non-FF pushes anyway... actually after a successful rebase the push CAN still be rejected if something merged in between (tiny window). That's handled by the `if !` warning. # Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"

          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The direct-push approach is a reasonable trade (bypass actor + rebase-first + no force-push + soft-fail on rejection), and the concurrency group + ledger-excluded affected-set logic keep it safe from double-releases. Two real regressions versus the PR flow it replaces, plus stale docs — none blocking.

**Key Issues**:
- The ledger commit lost its `[skip ci]` tag, so the direct push to main re-triggers this workflow on every release (a redundant no-op run queued behind the concurrency group — the old comment at line 138 documents exactly this hazard).
- `git rebase origin/main` under `set -euo pipefail` hard-fails the whole release if main moves mid-run, contradicting the "rejected push warns" soft-fail design adopted one line below.

- Operational note: the push only lands if the credential is the ruleset bypass actor (ai-teammate app, Integration 5153011). If `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is unset/a user PAT and `GITHUB_TOKEN` (github-actions[bot]) is not in the bypass list, every push is rejected and the workflow silently degrades to warn-only — releases publish, the ledger never lands. Verify the token identity once.

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `[skip ci]` to the ledger commit message (`git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci]"`).
2. Make the rebase soft-fail (`|| { warn; git rebase --abort; exit 0; }`) to match the push-rejection handling.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Ledger push re-triggers this workflow — `[skip ci]` was dropped**

The old squash-merge flow deliberately put `[skip ci]` in the merge subject; the comment that used to sit here said exactly why: *"The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not cover versions.json)."* The direct push at this line pushes the ledger commit `chore(release): bump agent versions` — no skip keyword — straight to `main`, which is a push event on a non-ignored path.

Consequences of the re-triggered run: it is serialized behind this run by the `agent-pack-release` concurrency group, and by the time it starts the new release tag exists, so `base...HEAD` covers only the versions.json bump. `isAgentConfigFile` excludes the ledger and `setupTouched()` is false, so the run ends as a `.no-release` no-op — **not** a double-release. But every release now burns a full queued runner cycle (checkout, node setup, dmtools install) and queues behind the group, delaying the next real release — precisely the gate-waste this PR set out to eliminate.

Fix is one word at the commit step (~line 167):

```bash
git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci]"
```

(`[skip ci]` in the commit message skips push-triggered runs, which is how the squash flow avoided this.)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `git rebase` hard-fails the release in the race the PR says is safe**

This step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `git rebase origin/main` fails — e.g. main moved in the seconds between the guard-1 fetch and this rebase and `versions.json` conflicts — the step exits non-zero and the **whole release fails**: the packs are built but the GitHub Release never publishes, the ledger never lands, and nothing re-runs it (the next release only recomputes when some future push triggers the workflow). That is the same race window the code handles gracefully one line below (`if ! git push ...` → warn and move on), and it contradicts both the PR description ("rejected push warns and the next release recomputes") and the pre-existing "never fail the release" design principle documented in this file.

Note the old flow survived this exact race: the version PR was simply left open for the machine loop while the release still published.

Make the rebase soft-fail the same way:

```bash
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
  echo "::warning::ledger rebase conflicted — main moved; aborting the ledger bump, the release still publishes and the next release recomputes from main"
  git rebase --abort
  git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
  exit 0
fi
```

(`git rebase --abort` also restores the repo so the failure path doesn't leave a rebase-in-progress state, and the remote reset avoids leaving the token-embedded URL behind.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: duplicate `git fetch origin main`**

Guard 1 (line 170) runs the identical `git fetch origin main` a few lines earlier, immediately before the `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` check. Keeping a fetch right before the rebase is good practice (it narrows the non-fast-forward race), but two fetches of the same ref within seconds are redundant. Consider dropping the fetch from guard 1 and keeping this one, or reusing guard 1's fetch and accepting the slightly wider race here — one fetch per concern is enough.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Ledger push re-triggers this workflow — `[skip ci]` was dropped**

The old squash-merge flow deliberately put `[skip ci]` in the merge subject; the comment that used to sit here said exactly why: *"The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not cover versions.json)."* The direct push at this line pushes the ledger commit `chore(release): bump agent versions` — no skip keyword — straight to `main`, which is a push event on a non-ignored path.

Consequences of the re-triggered run: it is serialized behind this run by the `agent-pack-release` concurrency group, and by the time it starts the new release tag exists, so `base...HEAD` covers only the versions.json bump. `isAgentConfigFile` excludes the ledger and `setupTouched()` is false, so the run ends as a `.no-release` no-op — **not** a double-release. But every release now burns a full queued runner cycle (checkout, node setup, dmtools install) and queues behind the group, delaying the next real release — precisely the gate-waste this PR set out to eliminate.

Fix is one word at the commit step (~line 167):

```bash
git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci]"
```

(`[skip ci]` in the commit message skips push-triggered runs, which is how the squash flow avoided this.)
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `git rebase` hard-fails the release in the race the PR says is safe**

This step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `git rebase origin/main` fails — e.g. main moved in the seconds between the guard-1 fetch and this rebase and `versions.json` conflicts — the step exits non-zero and the **whole release fails**: the packs are built but the GitHub Release never publishes, the ledger never lands, and nothing re-runs it (the next release only recomputes when some future push triggers the workflow). That is the same race window the code handles gracefully one line below (`if ! git push ...` → warn and move on), and it contradicts both the PR description ("rejected push warns and the next release recomputes") and the pre-existing "never fail the release" design principle documented in this file.

Note the old flow survived this exact race: the version PR was simply left open for the machine loop while the release still published.

Make the rebase soft-fail the same way:

```bash
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
  echo "::warning::ledger rebase conflicted — main moved; aborting the ledger bump, the release still publishes and the next release recomputes from main"
  git rebase --abort
  git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
  exit 0
fi
```

(`git rebase --abort` also restores the repo so the failure path doesn't leave a rebase-in-progress state, and the remote reset avoids leaving the token-embedded URL behind.)
