# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

blocks.text:
Now let me analyze this PR carefully. It's a workflow change to `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml`. The change replaces the chore PR path (branch + PR + wait for checks + merge) with a direct push to main using a ruleset bypass actor.

Key observations:

1. **Workflow/CI safety dimension** is critical here.

2. The step name and comment are now stale: the step is named `"Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"` and the big comment block above still describes the PR-based approach ("Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors... the bump rides a side branch + PR + squash merge... Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): ... wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch..."). This is dead/misleading documentation. The step name references "via PR" which no longer happens. This is an IMPORTANT maintainability issue.

3. **Duplicate `git fetch origin main`**: Guard 1 already runs `git fetch origin main` just before. The new code does `git fetch origin main` again immediately after. Redundant. SUGGESTION.

4. **The push doesn't verify what it pushes**: Previously guard 2 re-checked `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` after waiting for checks. Now after `git rebase origin/main`, it pushes HEAD:main unconditionally — the rebase may succeed and the pushes whatever HEAD is, which includes the versions.json bump commit. Wait — after rebase onto origin/main, HEAD contains main + the bump commit, so push is fast-forward. That's fine. But what if the rebase introduces conflicts? `git rebase origin/main` — since the only local commit is the versions.json bump commit on top of fetched main, and we fetched origin/main in guard 1, the rebase should be trivial. If there were a conflict, rebase would fail with non-zero exit and `set -euo pipefail` would kill the step — release fails after packs are published but before the ledger lands and before the GitHub Release is created. Hmm, is that a failure mode? The old code's philosophy was "never fail the release AFTER publishing". Here the release (GitHub Release publish) happens in the NEXT step, so failing here means no release published — actually failing here means packs were built but no release published and no ledger landed. The old comment said "never fail the release AFTER publishing" — the ledger push happens BEFORE "Publish the GitHub Release". So failing the step on rebase conflict means the release never publishes even though packs were built. But with the concurrency group and fetch right before, conflicts are near-impossible unless... actually the local HEAD after `git reset --hard origin/main` in the "Sync to current main" step, plus one commit. Rebase onto freshly fetched origin/main — the delta is commits that landed between. Conflict on versions.json possible if two releases ran concurrently? Concurrency group serializes them, so no. Manual dispatch targeting non-main ref could... but then the guard `git diff HEAD origin/main` might pass or not. Edge-case.

Actually wait — more significant: with `set -euo pipefail`, if `git rebase origin/main` fails (conflict), the step fails → workflow fails → release NOT published → next push re-triggers. Is that bad? The PR description says "rejected push warns and the next release recomputes" — but a rebase conflict doesn't warn, it hard-fails. Given the fetch happens seconds before push, the window is tiny, and GitHub rejects non-FF pushes anyway... actually after a successful rebase the push CAN still be rejected if something merged in between (tiny window). That's handled by the `if !` warning. {"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Ledger push re-triggers this workflow — `[skip ci]` was dropped**

The old squash-merge flow deliberately put `[skip ci]` in the merge subject; the comment that used to sit here said exactly why: *"The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not cover versions.json)."* The direct push at this line pushes the ledger commit `chore(release): bump agent versions` — no skip keyword — straight to `main`, which is a push event on a non-ignored path.

Consequences of the re-triggered run: it is serialized behind this run by the `agent-pack-release` concurrency group, and by the time it starts the new release tag exists, so `base...HEAD` covers only the versions.json bump. `isAgentConfigFile` excludes the ledger and `setupTouched()` is false, so the run ends as a `.no-release` no-op — **not** a double-release. But every release now burns a full queued runner cycle (checkout, node setup, dmtools install) and queues behind the group, delaying the next real release — precisely the gate-waste this PR set out to eliminate.

Fix is one word at the commit step (~line 167):

```bash
git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci]"
```

(`[skip ci]` in the commit message skips push-triggered runs, which is how the squash flow avoided this.)

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `git rebase` hard-fails the release in the race the PR says is safe**

This step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `git rebase origin/main` fails — e.g. main moved in the seconds between the guard-1 fetch and this rebase and `versions.json` conflicts — the step exits non-zero and the **whole release fails**: the packs are built but the GitHub Release never publishes, the ledger never lands, and nothing re-runs it (the next release only recomputes when some future push triggers the workflow). That is the same race window the code handles gracefully one line below (`if ! git push ...` → warn and move on), and it contradicts both the PR description ("rejected push warns and the next release recomputes") and the pre-existing "never fail the release" design principle documented in this file.

Note the old flow survived this exact race: the version PR was simply left open for the machine loop while the release still published.

Make the rebase soft-fail the same way:

```bash
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
  echo "::warning::ledger rebase conflicted — main moved; aborting the ledger bump, the release still publishes and the next release recomputes from main"
  git rebase --abort
  git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
  exit 0
fi
```

(`git rebase --abort` also restores the repo so the failure path doesn't leave a rebase-in-progress state, and the remote reset avoids leaving the token-embedded URL behind.)

**What the PR does**: replaces the chore-PR ledger flow in `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml` with a direct push of the bumped `versions.json` to main, using a ruleset bypass actor, rebase-first, soft-fail on rejected push.

**Key findings** (all verified against `ci/release_packs.mjs` and `ci/pack_release_guard.cjs`):

1. **IMPORTANT** (inline, line 184) — the ledger commit lost its `[skip ci]` tag when the squash-merge path was deleted. The direct push re-triggers this workflow on every release; the concurrency group + ledger-excluded affected-set logic make the follow-up run a no-op rather than a double-release, but it still burns a full queued runner cycle per release — the exact gate-waste the PR claims to eliminate. One-word fix at the commit step.

2. **IMPORTANT** (inline, line 183) — `git rebase origin/main` runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so in the "main moved" race the PR describes as safe, the rebase hard-fails the whole release *before* publishing (packs built, release never ships). Inconsistent with the warn-and-continue push handling one line below and the file's "never fail the release" principle.

3. **SUGGESTION** (inline, line 182) — duplicate `git fetch origin main`; guard 1 fetched the same ref seconds earlier.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")

        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check

        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.

        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.

          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

blocks.text:
Now let me analyze this PR carefully. It's a workflow change to `.github/workflows/agent-pack-release.yml`. The change replaces the chore PR path (branch + PR + wait for checks + merge) with a direct push to main using a ruleset bypass actor.

Key observations:

1. **Workflow/CI safety dimension** is critical here.

2. The step name and comment are now stale: the step is named `"Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"` and the big comment block above still describes the PR-based approach ("Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors... the bump rides a side branch + PR + squash merge... Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): ... wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch..."). This is dead/misleading documentation. The step name references "via PR" which no longer happens. This is an IMPORTANT maintainability issue.

3. **Duplicate `git fetch origin main`**: Guard 1 already runs `git fetch origin main` just before. The new code does `git fetch origin main` again immediately after. Redundant. SUGGESTION.

4. **The push doesn't verify what it pushes**: Previously guard 2 re-checked `git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json` after waiting for checks. Now after `git rebase origin/main`, it pushes HEAD:main unconditionally — the rebase may succeed and the pushes whatever HEAD is, which includes the versions.json bump commit. Wait — after rebase onto origin/main, HEAD contains main + the bump commit, so push is fast-forward. That's fine. But what if the rebase introduces conflicts? `git rebase origin/main` — since the only local commit is the versions.json bump commit on top of fetched main, and we fetched origin/main in guard 1, the rebase should be trivial. If there were a conflict, rebase would fail with non-zero exit and `set -euo pipefail` would kill the step — release fails after packs are published but before the ledger lands and before the GitHub Release is created. Hmm, is that a failure mode? The old code's philosophy was "never fail the release AFTER publishing". Here the release (GitHub Release publish) happens in the NEXT step, so failing here means no release published — actually failing here means packs were built but no release published and no ledger landed. The old comment said "never fail the release AFTER publishing" — the ledger push happens BEFORE "Publish the GitHub Release". So failing the step on rebase conflict means the release never publishes even though packs were built. But with the concurrency group and fetch right before, conflicts are near-impossible unless... actually the local HEAD after `git reset --hard origin/main` in the "Sync to current main" step, plus one commit. Rebase onto freshly fetched origin/main — the delta is commits that landed between. Conflict on versions.json possible if two releases ran concurrently? Concurrency group serializes them, so no. Manual dispatch targeting non-main ref could... but then the guard `git diff HEAD origin/main` might pass or not. Edge-case.

Actually wait — more significant: with `set -euo pipefail`, if `git rebase origin/main` fails (conflict), the step fails → workflow fails → release NOT published → next push re-triggers. Is that bad? The PR description says "rejected push warns and the next release recomputes" — but a rebase conflict doesn't warn, it hard-fails. Given the fetch happens seconds before push, the window is tiny, and GitHub rejects non-FF pushes anyway... actually after a successful rebase the push CAN still be rejected if something merged in between (tiny window). That's handled by the `if !` warning. The rebase-conflict case: extremely unlikely given the local branch is main + one versions.json commit and origin/main was just fetched; a conflict requires versions.json to have changed on main in the seconds between fetch and rebase — basically the same race as push rejection. But it would fail hard instead of warning. Inconsistent with the stated "never fail after publishing" philosophy... though publishing happens after. Hmm, but if the step fails, the GitHub Release never publishes, so the built packs are lost and versions.json on main is not bumped — next run recomputes. Actually is that acceptable? The old code would leave a PR for the machine loop. I'd call this at most SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT: use `git rebase origin/main || { warn; exit 0; }` to match the soft-failure philosophy. Actually wait — exiting 0 there means the release publishes but ledger never lands → next release recomputes. That matches "rejected push warns" handling. I'd flag as SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT. Given the "never fail the release" design principle documented in the old comment, making rebase failure fatal is a behavioral deviation worth IMPORTANT... but the probability is minuscule. Let me think about the severity mapping: BLOCKING = correctness/bug. Is there an actual bug?

5. **Security concern — the bypass actor**: This workflow pushes directly to main bypassing branch protection. The token used is `secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. The PR description says the bypass was added to "Integration 5153011" (the ai-teammate app). If `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is a PAT from a different actor, the push would be rejected (not bypassed) — falls to the warning path. Fine.

Security consideration: direct push to main with `contents: write` and a token that bypasses rulesets. The pushed content is just the bot's own versions.json bump commit — the commit content is computed by `ci/release_packs.mjs`, not external input. Risk is low. But one subtle issue: after rebase, the pushes HEAD which is origin/main + bump commit — so it pushes everything on main, fine.

# Agent pack release (dmtools-agents#441).
#
# Builds and publishes per-agent versioned packs — one self-contained zip per
# affected agent (<agent>-<version>.zip + manifest.json + .sha256) — so
# consumers fetch a single agent over plain HTTPS instead of a git submodule.
#
# The pack format is built by `dmtools compile` (dm.ai#595) — the runtime repo
# owns the single implementation; this workflow only orchestrates: test →
# compute affected set → bump versions.json → compile → validate → publish.
#
# Triggers:
#   push to main            — affected set from the diff since the last release tag
#   workflow_dispatch       — manual; `agents=all` or `agents=name1,name2`,
#                             `bump` selects patch/minor/major (default patch)
name: Agent Pack Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      # CI-only changes never cut a release. NOTE: '**.md' is deliberately
      # NOT ignored — agent instruction packs ship .md files (instructions/
      # joined the default agents in a57b3ba); ignoring them let runner
      # configs reference pack files the published zips never carried
      # (live: 2026-10-01 dev-leg failure, story_development-0.1.11).
      - '.github/**'
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'site/**'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agents:
        description: "'all' or a comma-separated agent list (default: affected set)"
        required: false
        default: ''
      bump:
        description: 'Version bump'
        required: false
        default: 'patch'
        type: choice
        options: [patch, minor, major]
      dry_run:
        description: 'Build + validate without publishing'
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean

concurrency:
  group: agent-pack-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write # publish the GitHub Release + commit versions.json

jobs:
  release:
    # The JS unit-test suite is NOT re-run here (owner 2026-10-01): quality.yml
    # runs it on every PR and main's protection is strict (required `crap` +
    # up-to-date), so every commit reaching main already passed the suite on a
    # current head. The release only computes the affected set, compiles,
    # validates and publishes.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history for the since-last-release diff

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' resolves to the current release tag (owner mandate 2026-10-01).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        env:
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION || vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.22' }}
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Compute base ref (last release tag, if any)
        id: base
        run: |
          last_tag=$(git tag --list 'agents-rel-*' --sort=-creatordate | head -1)
          echo "ref=${last_tag}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "base ref: ${last_tag:-<none — first release, all agents>}"

      - name: Sync to current main (queued runs release current main)
        # The concurrency group serializes release runs, but actions/checkout
        # gives each run its own TRIGGER SHA — a run queued behind another
        # computed its affected set and version bumps from a ledger that
        # pre-dated the previous run's ledger PR (live 2026-10-04, gh-690:
        # three content PRs merged within 3 min → overlapping releases
        # double-bumped sm_github/pr_review to 0.1.24 and cut the empty
        # ledger PR #689). Reset to origin/main so base-tag...HEAD covers
        # exactly the unreleased content ONCE, from the current ledger; a
        # queued run that finds everything already released writes
        # dist/.no-release and no-ops. Gated to push events — a manual
        # dispatch may deliberately target a non-main ref.
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        run: |
          git fetch origin main
          git reset --hard origin/main

      - name: Build + validate affected agent packs
        id: build
        env:
          AGENTS: ${{ inputs.agents || '' }}
          BUMP: ${{ inputs.bump || 'patch' }}
          DRY: ${{ inputs.dry_run || false }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--out dist)
          [ -n "${AGENTS}" ] && args+=(--agents="${AGENTS}")
          [ -n "${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}" ] && args+=(--base-ref="${{ steps.base.outputs.ref }}")
          [ "${DRY}" = "true" ] && args+=(--dry-run)
          [ "${BUMP}" != "patch" ] && args+=(--bump="${BUMP}")
          node ci/release_packs.mjs "${args[@]}"
          # Signal "nothing to release" to the publish steps.
          if [ -f dist/.no-release ]; then echo "released=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; else echo "released=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

      - name: "Bump versions.json via PR (protection-clean)"
        # Rulesets on personal repos have no bypass actors and no PAT scope
        # can edit them from CI (HTTP 404, live 2026-10-01) — a direct push
        # to main can NEVER satisfy required checks. So the bump rides a
        # side branch + PR + squash merge: quality.yml's crap check
        # satisfies the ruleset. The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the
        # merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not
        # cover versions.json).
        #
        # Nothing-changed guard (gh-690): a server-side auto-merge fires the
        # moment the checks pass and cannot re-verify that main did not move
        # while the PR waited — #689 merged with a 0-byte diff because its
        # branch was cut before the previous ledger PR landed. Instead: skip
        # creating the PR when main already carries the target versions
        # (guard 1), wait for the checks with gh pr checks --watch, re-run
        # the guard (guard 2), and CLOSE the PR when the diff went empty.
        # Only a still-different ledger merges; a diverged one (conflict) is
        # left for the machine loop rather than failing the release AFTER
        # publishing.
        if: steps.build.outputs.released == 'true' && inputs.dry_run != true
        env:
          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          origin_url="https://x-access-token:[REDACTED:Connection String Password]@github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
          git remote set-url origin "$origin_url"
          # Commit FIRST (compile rewrote versions.json — unstaged tracked
          # files make later operations refuse).
          git add versions.json
          git diff --cached --quiet && exit 0
          git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions"
          # Guard 1 — main may already carry the target versions when an
          # earlier run's ledger PR merged while this run sat in the
          # concurrency queue (gh-690): skip creating the PR entirely.
          git fetch origin main
          if git diff --quiet HEAD origin/main -- versions.json; then
            echo "::notice::main already carries the target agent versions — no ledger PR needed"
            git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSI…

The old squash-merge flow deliberately put `[skip ci]` in the merge subject; the comment that used to sit here said exactly why: *"The squash subject carries [skip ci] so the merge push does not re-trigger a release (paths-ignore does not cover versions.json)."* The direct push at this line pushes the ledger commit `chore(release): bump agent versions` — no skip keyword — straight to `main`, which is a push event on a non-ignored path.

Consequences of the re-triggered run: it is serialized behind this run by the `agent-pack-release` concurrency group, and by the time it starts the new release tag exists, so `base...HEAD` covers only the versions.json bump. `isAgentConfigFile` excludes the ledger and `setupTouched()` is false, so the run ends as a `.no-release` no-op — **not** a double-release. But every release now burns a full queued runner cycle (checkout, node setup, dmtools install) and queues behind the group, delaying the next real release — precisely the gate-waste this PR set out to eliminate.

git commit -m "chore(release): bump agent versions [skip ci]"
```

(`[skip ci]` in the commit message skips push-triggered runs, which is how the squash flow avoided this.)

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `git rebase` hard-fails the release in the race the PR says is safe**

This step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so if `git rebase origin/main` fails — e.g. main moved in the seconds between the guard-1 fetch and this rebase and `versions.json` conflicts — the step exits non-zero and the **whole release fails**: the packs are built but the GitHub Release never publishes, the ledger never lands, and nothing re-runs it (the next release only recomputes when some future push triggers the workflow). That is the same race window the code handles gracefully one line below (`if ! git push ...` → warn and move on), and it contradicts both the PR description ("rejected push warns and the next release recomputes") and the pre-existing "never fail the release" design principle documented in this file.

Note the old flow survived this exact race: the version PR was simply left open for the machine loop while the release still published.

Make the rebase soft-fail the same way:

```bash
if ! git rebase origin/main; then
  echo "::warning::ledger rebase conflicted — main moved; aborting the ledger bump, the release still publishes and the next release recomputes from main"
  git rebase --abort
  git remote set-url origin "https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}.git"
  exit 0
fi
```

(`git rebase --abort` also restores the repo so the failure path doesn't leave a rebase-in-progress state, and the remote reset avoids leaving the token-embedded URL behind.)
